propositions: The N=3000 import benchmark calls author() 6,000 times, each invoking subprocess-backed git config user.name lookup (47.79s cumulative), despite the author value remaining constant across an entire import.

The batch_stage_and_commit path calls stage_event for each new CREATE ticket, triggering sweep_stale_staging once per item (3,000 sweeps with 375,876 owner checks totaling 15.94s), despite the same staging root being rescanned identically within a single bounded batch.

Controlled identical-state A/B testing shows replacing only the git-config and sweep collaborators with side-effect-free logical equivalents (while retaining 3,000 creates, 3,000 comments, and 24 commits) reduced wall time from 77.23s to 16.40s, a 60.83s delta (78.8%) that discriminates these mechanisms from event serialization or commit-count changes.

The accepted benchmark contract (left-changeful-mamba) locks N=3000, 6,000 events, exactly 24 crash-safe commits, ≥10x reduction, complete counts, rollback, and resume; no ticket rejects caching user.name within an explicit import context or limiting stale-staging sweeps to one per batch chunk.
Interactive/direct writes must retain live author lookup and per-event stale-staging behavior; cache and batch optimizations must not leak across independent calls, threads, tasks, or test sessions.

The optimization must preserve event bytes, author fallback semantics, crash-resume, rollback, atomic staging/publish, commit structure, and all platform/Python version coverage without weakening any test or external behavior contract.
